language.script_notes: Cyrillic-only on official signage, no Latin transliteration alongside it (unlike some other Cyrillic-using countries that dual-post). Distinguishing it from Russian/Ukrainian/Serbian Cyrillic by eye alone is hard — lean on other clues, not the alphabet, to separate Bulgaria from its Cyrillic neighbors.

road_furniture.bollard_color: White post with a red rectangle reflector on the front face and a white rectangle on the back face.
road_furniture.guardrail_type: Standard European w-beam guardrail on rural highways; not a strong distinguishing feature on its own.
road_furniture.line_paint: White lane lines, consistent with most of Eastern Europe — not diagnostic by itself.
road_furniture.curb_style: No strongly distinctive curb style noted; roads are frequently in poor condition with visible potholes and uneven surfaces outside major routes.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Utility poles are often concrete, sometimes with the 'holey pole' look also seen elsewhere in Eastern Europe — not unique to Bulgaria.

architecture.roof_style: No single dominant iconic roofline; general Eastern Bloc-influenced mix.
architecture.wall_construction: Concrete block and plaster common, especially Soviet-era apartment blocks in cities.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Muted, often weathered pastel or bare concrete tones.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Notable Soviet-era prefabricated apartment blocks in urban areas; rural areas often look visibly less prosperous than Western/Central Europe.

nature.vegetation: Deciduous forest in hill/mountain regions; agricultural plains in the north and south.
nature.terrain: Mixed — Balkan mountain ranges plus flat agricultural lowlands (Danubian Plain, Thracian Plain).
nature.climate_signature: Notably heavy winter Street View coverage — bare/dead trees and snow are common even outside deep winter, more so than most of the rest of Europe. This 'bleak' look is itself a mild tell.

vehicles.plate_color: Standard EU-format white plates with blue EU strip.
vehicles.plate_format: Standard EU format, not individually diagnostic.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: All licensed taxis are legally required to be yellow. No other strong car-based meta — occasional duct-tape 'flag' on car antennas is an Eastern-Europe-wide signal, not Bulgaria-specific.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mixed generations; not a primary diagnostic without more specific research.
google_coverage.blur_style: Standard Google blurring, nothing unusual noted.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Google car is white (unlike Russia/Ukraine, which use different liveries in places) — useful only as a negative signal, not a positive Bulgaria confirmation.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic script, Eastern European road infrastructure feel
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Russia's Google car livery and road/vehicle meta differ; Bulgaria's bollards (red/white flat post) are a specific, checkable tell Russia doesn't share.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic visible in places, similar Balkan terrain and road quality
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Serbia mixes Latin and Cyrillic signage and has its own distinct bollard pattern (off-center red rectangle); Bulgaria is Cyrillic-only on official signage.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Balkan terrain, Cyrillic script, similar economic/infrastructure feel
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Check bollard design and sign-color conventions (blue for larger cities, white for villages in Bulgaria) as the tiebreak rather than terrain.
